claims.text: The initial eutectic high-entropy alloy has dual-phase lamellar colonies with numerous internal boundaries.
Microcracking initiates at internal lamellar-colony boundaries during room-temperature tensile deformation.
A controlled post-solidification annealing treatment can induce nanoscale precipitates at lamellar-colony interfaces.
The proposed precipitates will be coherent.
Nanoscale precipitates will obstruct dislocation motion.
Obstructing dislocation motion with the precipitates will increase tensile strength.
The precipitates will act as crack-deflection sites.
The precipitates will act as crack-bridging sites.
Crack deflection and bridging by the precipitates will mitigate microcrack initiation and propagation.
Mitigating microcrack initiation and propagation will improve room-temperature tensile ductility.
The annealed alloy will have higher tensile strength than the unmodified lamellar-colony baseline.
The annealed alloy will have greater room-temperature tensile ductility than the unmodified lamellar-colony baseline.
The unmodified eutectic high-entropy alloy is brittle at room temperature because of microcracking along internal lamellar-colony boundaries.
The intervention will be effective only when annealing produces an appropriate precipitate size, distribution, and coherency at colony boundaries.
The intervention may be ineffective in alloys with substantially different microstructures.
